text:
sasha: FYI — legal routed a DSAR that asks for account export + deletion of all attachments (pptx, zip, screenshots). It looks like attachments live in S3 with envelope encryption. Question: what's our verification + delete flow for attachment blobs vs embeddings? cc @legal @privacy

mike: Do we currently treat attachments as part of the subject's data for erasure? I thought embeddings + convo transcripts were covered, not large binary blobs.

ada: we should — attachments can contain PII. Our erase policy in theory covers any data tied to the subject_id. The tricky part is attachments in backups & immutable snapshots.

lex: infra notes: attachments are stored under tenant/<tenant-id>/objects/<object-id>. Objects are encrypted with envelope encryption: CEK per-tenant, CEK wrapped by KMS. Deleting S3 objects + deleting key material should make them unrecoverable for normal ops, but backups/snapshots are a concern.

mike: so practical steps: 1) validate requester (legal already did?), 2) lock account to prevent new uploads, 3) queue s3 delete for prefix, 4) rotate/revoke CEK? 5) kick off snapshot reclamation. Is that right?

sasha: legal confirmed identity verification done in portal. They also flagged attachments might appear in a shared folder used by multiple users. We need to avoid deleting other users' files.

ada: important: we must correlate attachment ownership. Object metadata includes uploader_id and subject_ids we observed during ingestion. If shared, we need to only delete references and redaction, not always remove the object. We also have to keep an audit trail.

lex: implementation detail: our object store has reference counts in metadata db. Flow suggestion:
```
# proposed erase flow for attachments
1. Verify DSAR ticket & requester ID
2. Lock subject uploads
3. Lookup objects where metadata.uploader_id == subject_id OR metadata.subject_ids contains subject_id
4a. If object.refcount == 1 -> enqueue S3 delete job + mark for CEK revoke
4b. If refcount > 1 -> scrub subject-specific metadata and create redaction marker (do not delete blob)
5. Create audit record with job ids and keystore op ids
6. Kick snapshot invalidation job for windows that include these objects
```

mike: how do we revoke CEKs safely? If we revoke the wrapping key in KMS, other tenants using same CEK would be affected. We need granular keys.

lex: we use per-tenant CEKs today; for older tenants we have a shared CEK bucket for legacy accounts. For legacy ones we need retention exception or manual forensics.

ada: legal says we must provide evidence of deletion. So we need an audit artifact showing: object IDs, delete job ID, S3 delete confirmation, keystore revoke ID, and snapshot purge ticket.

sasha: question for security: can we rely solely on CEK revocation as proof? Or do we need to actually delete S3 objects as well?

mike: CEK revocation is strong for confidentiality, but legal will want deletion receipts. S3 delete + version delete + lifecycle enforcement + CEK rotation is ideal. Also collect S3 DeleteMarker and AWS response.

lex: for backups: retention windows may keep data for 30/90 days. We'll need to open a retention-exception request for legal with backups team. That should be an escalated IR ticket (backup-purge) and documented.

dsar-bot: DSAR ticket created: DSAR-2026-0421. Attached: initial verification, scope list, requestor contact. Please update thread when you enqueue delete jobs.

ada: edge-case: attachments in third-party integrations (google drive links) — we only store pointers. For those we need to send a takedown request to integration owner and document the action.

mike: owners: lex -> s3 delete job + CEK revoke plan; ada -> audit artifact template + legal liaison; sasha -> confirm scope and shared-object rules. Can we aim to have first-pass delete plan by EOD tomorrow?

lex: I can sketch the delete job and the DB queries by EOD. For legacy shared CEKs I'll flag the tenant ids so legal can decide exemption.

ada: I'll draft the audit evidence format. We should include the following fields: object_id, bucket/key, uploader_id, delete_job_id, s3_response, keystore_key_id, kms_disable_request_id, snapshot_purge_ticket.

sasha: also add: anonymization/redaction log entry if object not deleted but references scrubbed.

mike: one more: we must update our DSAR runbook to cover attachments explicitly and include the CEK/shared-key exception path. File a follow-up PR for the runbook after this case.

sasha: thanks team. tagging this thread for privacy audit later. If anyone hits a blocker (legacy CEKs or snapshot retention) escalate to @eng-sre.

lex: noted. I'll post the DB query and job prototype in this thread once done. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — please cc dsar-bot ticket when updates are submitted.

(END)
